input: Sign my kid up for a coding bootcamp

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The child's age and current skill level determines which bootcamps are age-appropriate and pitched at the right difficulty — beginner programs differ vastly from intermediate ones.
The programming language or topic focus (e.g. Scratch, Python, web dev, game design) narrows the search to relevant programs and avoids wasting time on mismatched ones.
Whether the bootcamp is in-person or online changes which programs are even available and affects the logistics of attendance entirely.
The desired start date or enrollment deadline determines urgency and filters out programs that don't fit the timeline.
Coding bootcamps range from free to thousands of dollars; knowing the budget rules out or prioritizes entire categories of programs.
Schedule format preferences (e.g. weekend, after-school, week-long intensive, summer camp) affect which programs are practical and sustainable for the child and family.
Knowing the main goal — fun and exploration, building a specific project, gaining a credential, or preparing for a career path — determines which program outcomes to prioritize.

gold.taskTitle: Sign kid up for a coding bootcamp
gold.taskDescription: Find and enroll the user's child in a suitable coding bootcamp program.

questions.title: How old is your child, and what is their coding experience?
questions.description: Understand the child's age and current skill level to identify age-appropriate and correctly pitched bootcamp programs.

questions.title: Is there a specific coding topic or language you want covered?
questions.description: Determine whether there is a preferred focus area such as Scratch, Python, web development, or game design to narrow down relevant programs.

questions.title: Should the bootcamp be in-person or are you open to online?
questions.description: Establish the delivery format to filter programs by availability and practical accessibility for your family.

questions.title: When do you want the bootcamp to start or be completed by?
questions.description: Identify the target start date or deadline to assess urgency and eliminate programs that fall outside the needed timeframe.

questions.title: What is your budget for this bootcamp?
questions.description: Clarify the spending limit to filter out programs that are too costly and surface free or affordable alternatives if needed.

questions.title: What schedule format works best — after-school, weekends, or an intensive?
questions.description: Understand scheduling preferences to identify programs whose time commitment is sustainable for the child and family routine.

questions.title: What is the main goal — fun, a project, a credential, or career prep?
questions.description: Define what a successful outcome looks like to prioritize programs whose outcomes and teaching style best match the family's expectations.
